solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Around hospital, pick out centre of dead plant

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for around

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of pick are jumbled
the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the inner pair of dead

explanation.surface: Someone at a hospital is told to remove the core of a dead plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PICK to ICKP; 'centre of' takes EA from the middle of dEAd.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea is a leguminous plant grown for its edible seeds.

clue.text: Toil here ruined one with pension?

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of toil here are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A worker complains that toiling here has ruined a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pension' is not retirement money but the French word for a boarding house, which this person runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension is a small continental guesthouse, and its keeper is a hotel proprietor.

clue.text: Am I not able to celebrate rising support?

parts.note: contracted, am I not able becomes can't I

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for celebrate is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate noisily

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud whether they are barred from joining a celebration of rising support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns REVEL into LEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam or bracket that holds up a balcony or bridge span.

clue.text: Except for end esplanade is in very ordinary condition

indicators.note: all of the word for esplanade except its last letter is kept

parts.note: a prom, short for promenade, is a seaside esplanade

indicators.note: in means the word is sits within the letters for very and ordinary

parts.note: O stands for Ordinary, as in the old British O level exam

explanation.surface: Apart from its far end, a seafront promenade is in a very mediocre state.
explanation.walkthrough: A prom is a British seaside promenade; ordinary gives O from the old British O level exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or condition attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Fruity variety of crab

parts.note: the crab here is not a crustacean but the crab tree, whose small sour fruit gives the full name of the answer when crab is put before it

explanation.surface: A seafood menu seems to offer a crab with a fruity flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a kind of crustacean, but crab is also the wild tree whose sour fruit is the crab apple.
explanation.definitionFit: The crab apple is a small wild variety of the orchard fruit, so this fruit is what crab qualifies.

clue.text: Physicist's wildly romantic time away

indicators.note: wildly means the letters of romantic are thrown about into a new order
away says one piece is gone from the letters before they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist spends a wildly romantic holiday away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes T out of ROMANTIC, and 'wildly' rearranges what is left, ROMANIC, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian physicist and engineer who pioneered radio telegraphy.

clue.text: Feign slap

definitions.meaning: to invent or fabricate, as a story or excuse
slap is British theatrical slang for cosmetics or greasepaint

explanation.surface: An instruction to fake being hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slap' looks like a blow, but in British slang it is face paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up a tale is to feign it, and make-up is the cosmetics actors call slap.

clue.text: Window crafted from iron set of tables by artist

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a nest of tables is a set that stacks one under another
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A window made from iron by an artist, along with a set of tables.
explanation.walkthrough: A nest is a set of small tables that slide under each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenestra is the Latin word for window, used in anatomy for an opening in bone.

clue.text: Friend managed team, putting fun first

indicators.note: putting, with first, places the word for fun ahead of the rest
first, with putting, says the word for fun comes at the front

parts.note: play is fun or amusement

indicators.note: managed means handled or arranged, so the letters of team are reordered

explanation.surface: A pal ran the team but cared more about enjoying the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges TEAM to MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a childhood companion, a friend to play with.

clue.text: Song and dance over drunk

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss, as is a stink
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone sings and dances after having a few too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' is a single idiom meaning a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinko is slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: Loved piece about early form of transport

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of loved piece are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cherished article on a historic means of getting around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The velocipede was an early pedal-powered bicycle of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Silly tenor taken in by trick starts to sing soprano

indicators.note: taken in by means the letter for tenor is enclosed by the word for trick

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: the starts of the words sing and soprano give their first letters

explanation.surface: A foolish tenor is tricked into singing the soprano part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' looks like 'deceived', which suits trick, but it puts T inside WILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Witless means lacking sense, foolish.

clue.text: King drowned in northbound river shoot

indicators.note: drowned in means put inside the water, here the letters of the river
in a down clue, northbound means the river's name is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king drowns in a river flowing north during a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northbound' turns TEES into SEET, and 'drowned in' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeet is a form of clay-pigeon shooting, so it names a type of shoot.

clue.text: Kid runs off in street for a scrap

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word for kid inside the letters for street
off means removed, so the letter for runs is dropped

parts.note: a nipper is a small child
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A child runs off into the street to join a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs off' takes R from NIPPER, leaving NIPPE. 'scrap' looks like a fight but means a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment, just as a scrap is.

clue.text: Brat makes progress essentially

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the answer lies within the words makes progress

explanation.surface: A spoilt child is fundamentally getting ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child, here a brat.

clue.text: A compiler with imagination meets resistance — one publishes abroad!

indicators.note: treated with imagination, the letters of a compiler are creatively rearranged

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An inventive crossword setter faces opposition and takes their work overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' means far and wide, not overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A proclaimer announces things publicly, and to publish abroad is to spread news widely.

clue.text: Yes, at heart, tapir is an animal

parts.note: OK is an affirmative, like yes

indicators.note: at heart means the middle letters of tapir are taken

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that a tapir counts as an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes API from the middle of tAPIr.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African mammal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Secrecy when account goes missing? That's a convenience

indicators.note: goes missing means the letters for account are removed

parts.note: privacy is secrecy or seclusion

explanation.surface: Without an account, privacy is lost, which suits some people.
explanation.walkthrough: A convenience is a British word for a public lavatory, as is a privy.
explanation.definitionFit: A privy is an outdoor toilet, and a convenience is a British euphemism for a lavatory.

clue.text: Reportedly top American voiced disapproval in child's game

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the word for top is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a peak is a top or summit
to boo is to voice disapproval

explanation.surface: A leading American is said to have jeered at a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns PEAK into PEEK, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is the game of hiding the face and revealing it to amuse a baby.

clue.text: Follow parent's beliefs

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular word that is used collectively for a body of beliefs

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
ma is an informal word for mother, a parent

explanation.surface: Advice to adopt one's parents' convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down as incontrovertibly true.

clue.text: Meeting about long novel using one language

indicators.note: about means the word for meeting goes round the rest

parts.note: a moot is an assembly or meeting

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of long are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A meeting discusses a lengthy novel written in a single language.
explanation.walkthrough: A moot is an old English word for an assembly, still used for a debating session.
explanation.definitionFit: A monoglot speaks or writes only one tongue.

clue.text: Poor keep having nothing in for tea

indicators.note: in puts the letter for nothing inside the rearranged letters
poor means badly made, so the letters of keep are disordered

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone poor can afford to keep nothing in for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges KEEP to PEKE, and O goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pekoe is a high-quality black tea made from young leaves.

clue.text: Dad's banter about model

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
to rag someone is to tease them with banter
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A father's joking concerns a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Share funny books in The Listener's range

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters of share are altered

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Share amusing books within The Listener crossword series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Listener' looks like the famous crossword, but it is simply anyone listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which a sound can be heard.

clue.text: A setter worked out a true copy

indicators.note: worked out means solved or reshaped, so the letters of a setter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword setter produces a faithful copy.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, an estreat is a certified extract or copy of a court record, especially of a fine.

clue.text: Sailor follows sailor — one's intimidating

indicators.note: follows puts one word after the other

parts.note: a second tar, another sailor
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: One sailor trails another, who is a fearsome figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a fierce, formidable person who is hard to deal with.

clue.text: Horse, we hear, goes around exhausted — that's annoying

indicators.note: goes around puts the letters for horse on either side of the word for exhausted
we hear means the horse word is spoken, and written as the letters that sound like it

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
all in means exhausted

explanation.surface: A horse said to be worn out keeps circling, which is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: GG is said gee-gee, a child's word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Galling means vexing or exasperating.

clue.text: Note by very loud singer at first is annoying

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of singer is used

explanation.surface: A very loud note from a singer is irritating at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Miffs means offends or irritates, as a present-tense verb.

clue.text: High-flying stunts from returning voluntary force during exercise

indicators.note: during means the reversed letters sit within the word for exercise

parts.note: aerobics is a form of exercise

indicators.note: returning means the letters for the force are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Stunt flying displays come from a volunteer unit back from training.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobatics are spectacular manoeuvres performed by aircraft in flight.

clue.text: It's comfortable in the outskirts of Londonderry

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters, here from Londonderry

explanation.surface: Life is cosy on the edge of Londonderry, a city in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but means at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Homely in British usage means cosy and welcoming, simple and comfortable.

clue.text: Occasionally working with old fellows

parts.note: on means working, as a switched-on machine is
and means together with
F is fellow, so FF is fellows

explanation.surface: Someone works only now and then alongside elderly colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: On and off means intermittently, from time to time.

clue.text: Thoroughly wet when most of planet's destroyed

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the planet is dropped

parts.note: Saturn is a planet
ate, as in ate away, means destroyed or consumed

explanation.surface: A planet is mostly wiped out in a deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims SATURN to SATUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak something completely.
